Abstract 
The Hospital Management System is a server rendered Django application that brings 
outpatient administrative and clinical workflows into a common relational data model. Four 
user roles support patient self service, doctor consultation work, front desk coordination and 
hospital administration. Shared authentication identifies users by email, optionally adds an 
email one time password, and routes users to their permitted portal. 
The implementation includes patient profiles, doctor availability, appointment booking, 
prescriptions with medicine lines, consultation and no show bills, notifications, receipts and 
administrator reports in HTML, CSV and PDF. The patient checkout is a simulation and does 
not charge a payment gateway. The data model supports MySQL configuration, an SQLite 
fallback and a documented PostgreSQL deployment option. 
Thirteen existing automated tests passed in an isolated SQLite environment on 20 October 
2026. These results establish the checked workflows and redirects in that environment; live 
MySQL concurrency, external email delivery and full browser validation remain separate 
acceptance activities. The report explains the implemented design, its practical limits and the 
improvements required before wider operational use.

1 Introduction 
The Hospital Management System organises the information used by patients, doctors, 
receptionists and administrators during outpatient care. Its purpose is to reduce the effort 
involved in finding patient records, coordinating consultation slots and maintaining consistent 
appointment and billing information. The application provides a single web interface with a 
different portal for each role. 
The project uses Django views and templates rather than a separate single page frontend and 
public REST service. Requests pass through framework middleware, URL routing and role 
checks before a view reads or changes records through the Django object relational mapper. 
HTML pages, small JSON responses, downloadable reports and email notifications form the 
main outputs. 
The discussion in this chapter establishes the problem, objectives and boundaries of the 
application. Later chapters connect those objectives to specific requirements, database 
entities, interface screens, implementation decisions and test evidence. The intended context 
is an academic outpatient management application, not a complete replacement for every 
department of a hospital. 
1.1 Problem Definition 
A hospital visit involves several related records. A patient needs an identity and contact 
details; a doctor needs an available consultation time; the receptionist needs to know whether 
that time is already reserved; and the administrator needs a reliable view of activity and 
charges. When these records are maintained in separate registers or disconnected files, a 
change made by one person may not be visible to another person at the time it is needed. 
A paper appointment book can record a booking, but it does not automatically connect the 
booking to a patient profile, a consultation bill or a notification. Staff may have to copy the 
same name, date and doctor information more than once. Searching by telephone number or 
reviewing a patient's previous visits becomes dependent on the organisation of those records. 
These are problem assumptions motivating the project, not findings from a claimed field 
survey. 
Appointment scheduling is especially sensitive to stale information. Two people can select 
the same apparent opening before either person finishes booking. The application addresses 
this problem by calculating slots from the doctor's schedule and checking again during final 
booking. A row lock on the doctor serialises supported booking operations on database 
engines with effective row locking. The appointment model itself does not declare a unique 
doctor, date and slot constraint. 
Access to clinical and financial information also requires boundaries. A patient should 
retrieve personal appointments and receipts; a doctor should retrieve patients linked to that 
doctor's appointments; and front desk staff need broader operational access without being 
allowed to change security policy. The project therefore uses a shared User identity with a 
role field and additional object filtering in relevant views.

The problem addressed is the coordination of these records and permissions in one 
application. It does not include inpatient bed allocation, laboratory processing, pharmacy 
inventory, insurance settlement or a real card payment service. Defining those exclusions 
prevents the report from describing a larger hospital information system than the source 
actually implements.

1.2 Objectives of the New System 
The primary objective is to connect outpatient administration and doctor consultation records 
through a common application. A booking should identify the patient and doctor, retain its 
date and time, expose its current status and provide a route to the associated financial record. 
The objective is consistency of workflow, rather than a numerical improvement unsupported 
by measurement. 
Functional objectives include patient self registration, assisted registration at reception, 
doctor discovery, date specific slot selection, appointment status management, consultation 
billing, no show handling, prescription entry and administrator reporting. Each objective 
maps to a current model or route. Staff creation belongs to the administrator portal; public 
registration creates patient accounts. 
The technical objectives are to use reusable framework services for authentication, database 
access and templates, and to centralise repeated concerns where practical. Slot generation 
belongs to Doctor.get_available_slots. Shared pagination, safe redirect handling and upload 
validation reduce duplicated rules across portals. Environment based configuration supports 
different database and mail settings without embedding deployment values in business views. 
Usability objectives are to give each role a focused dashboard, present lists with useful search 
and filters, display validation messages near an interrupted workflow and preserve 
predictable navigation after form submission. Reliability objectives include avoiding 
duplicate sequential bookings, keeping status changes visible across portals and providing 
repeatable automated checks. Security objectives include password hashing, optional OTP 
verification, CSRF middleware, authenticated sessions and ownership checks.

The expected outcome is a coherent academic demonstration of these workflows. 
Performance targets, operational uptime and regulatory compliance are not established by 
source inspection. They require explicit acceptance criteria, deployment configuration, 
measurement and organisational review.

1.3 Core Components 
Identity and security 
User stores email, role and OTP state. SystemSettings supplies the runtime OTP switch. 
Login, registration and password recovery are handled in patient/views.py for all roles. 
Authentication creates a framework session only after the enabled verification steps. The role 
then determines the destination portal; hiding a navigation item alone does not grant or deny 
access. 
Principal source files: accounts/models.py; patient/views.py 
Patient services 
Public information pages, self registration, profiles, doctor listing, appointment selection, 
checkout demonstration, personal bills and notifications. 
The pending booking is session data until checkout submission creates an appointment. 
Personal list and receipt views filter records through the logged in patient profile. 
Principal source files: patient/views.py; patient/dashboard_views.py 
Doctor services 
Availability, date exclusions, own appointments, own patients, diagnoses, prescriptions and 
medicine lines.

Doctor data is shared with booking and reporting. Clinical access is narrowed through 
appointments linked to the current doctor; prescription creation rechecks any linked 
appointment. 
Principal source files: doctor/models.py; doctor/views.py; doctor/patient_views.py 
Reception services 
Assisted patient registration, patient search, slot lookup, confirmed booking, status changes, 
billing and receipts. 
A receptionist booking immediately becomes confirmed and creates a pending consultation

Principal source files: receptionist/models.py; receptionist/views.py

Staff creation, account activation, hospital wide patient, appointment and billing lists,

1.5 Need for the New System 
The need for the application arises from the relationships among outpatient tasks. 
Registration is useful to appointment booking because it gives each visit a stable patient 
reference. Scheduling is useful to billing because a consultation fee can be derived from the 
selected doctor. A doctor benefits from seeing prior appointments and prescriptions in the 
same patient context. An administrator benefits from reports that read the same records used 
during daily work. 
Centralisation reduces the number of independent places where the same appointment status 
must be updated. When a receptionist confirms an appointment, the saved status can be read 
by the patient portal and doctor lists. The notification record also gives the patient a visible 
message. The application does not guarantee that email arrives or that the patient has read it; 
those are separate communication outcomes. 
The system is also needed as a structured academic implementation of role separation and 
relational modelling. The distinction between User and role profiles demonstrates reuse of a 
common identity. The separation of Prescription and PrescriptionMedicine demonstrates a 
one to many clinical record. Billing can contain both consultation and no show entries for a 
single appointment without embedding repeating charge fields in the appointment table.

1.6 Scope of the New System 
The functional scope covers outpatient patient administration, doctor scheduling, consultation 
appointments, basic clinical prescriptions, consultation charges and management reporting. 
The four role portals are the user facing boundaries. Public visitors can read information and 
use contact and authentication pages. Patient registration is public; staff account creation is an 
administrative operation. 
The data scope includes demographic and contact information, doctor professional details and 
fees, availability rules, appointments, diagnosis and advice, medicine lines, bills, notifications 
and contact submissions. Uploaded profile images are held in file storage and referenced by 
database fields. Framework tables additionally manage sessions, permissions, content types 
and administration history. 
Deployment scope includes a local development server and supplied Linux deployment 
templates. The design can be configured for different supported relational databases, but 
portability in configuration does not prove identical locking or operational performance. 
SMTP availability, network configuration, static file collection and media backup remain 
deployment responsibilities. 
The current patient routes do not include a dedicated prescription history page or a 
prescription download endpoint. Prescription entry and history are implemented in the doctor 
portal. Earlier descriptive documents may imply wider patient clinical access; that is treated 
as a proposed enhancement unless supported by a current route and view. 
The current version does not implement a laboratory information system, inpatient ward 
management, pharmacy stock control, insurance claims, real financial settlement, video 
consultation or an external electronic health record API. It also does not establish production 
service level objectives or a measured maximum user count. These boundaries keep 
implementation claims consistent with the available code.

1.7 Advantages and Limitations of the Proposed System 
The main advantage is that the system gives related tasks a common record structure. Patient 
identity, appointments and bills are joined through explicit relationships. The doctor sees a 
focused clinical workspace, while reception has the tools needed to organise daily visits. An 
administrator can inspect wider activity without duplicating operational data into another 
application. 
Shared slot computation is another advantage. Both patient and receptionist booking call the 
same method, so changes to blocked dates, working hours or slot duration affect both 
workflows. Cancelled appointments are excluded from occupied slot labels, allowing the 
corresponding time to be offered again. Missing weekday availability falls back to 09:00 to 
17:00; it does not mean that the doctor is closed. 
The project demonstrates several useful safeguards: framework password handling, CSRF 
middleware, role decorators, object filtering, name checks, image content verification and 
safe redirect validation. These are concrete controls, but they do not justify a claim that the 
whole application has passed a security audit. Several input flows still read POST values 
directly, and model choices alone do not validate arbitrary values when objects are created 
without full_clean. 
Reliability has important limits. In the booking views, the atomic block protects the doctor 
row and appointment creation. Bill and notification creation occur afterward. A later failure 
could therefore leave an appointment without the expected related output. Prescription and 
medicine creation also lack a single surrounding transaction in the inspected view. These are 
specific improvement opportunities rather than hypothetical features. 
Source level database relationships are helpful but do not cover every business invariant. 
Patient and employee identifiers are generated by inspecting the last row, which can race 
under concurrent creation. Billing duplicates the patient reference already available through 
Appointment, so the application must keep both references consistent. A future database and 
service review should define and enforce these invariants explicitly.

1.9 Target Users 
Patient 
A patient creates a self service account, maintains personal information, selects a doctor and 
date, checks available slots and follows the demonstration checkout. Personal appointment, 
billing and notification views keep the operational history accessible. A patient does not 
create staff accounts or change another patient record. 
Typical workflow: Register or login; complete OTP when enabled; open booking; select a 
free slot; review the fee; submit demo payment; inspect appointment and bill. 
Doctor 
A doctor manages professional profile information and scheduling rules, reviews assigned 
appointments, views related patients and writes prescriptions. Patient details are restricted 
through appointments associated with the current doctor. The role is clinical and scheduling 
oriented rather than responsible for global staff management. 
Typical workflow: Login; review today appointments; open an assigned patient; inspect 
history; record diagnosis and medicine lines; update the appointment; review prescription 
history. 
Receptionist 
A receptionist carries out assisted registration and front desk coordination. The portal 
supports patient search, direct confirmed bookings, confirmation and cancellation, no show 
handling, bill status updates and receipts. The registering receptionist is retained on a walk in 
patient profile where applicable. 
Typical workflow: Login; find or register the patient; inspect a doctor schedule; book a free 
slot; manage attendance; record payment and open the receipt.

Administrator 
The administrator manages hospital wide operational data and staff access. The portal 
supports doctor and receptionist creation, account activation controls, appointments, billing, 
reports and the singleton OTP policy. This role is distinct from the framework is_superuser 
flag even though an account can also possess Django administrative privileges. 
Typical workflow: Login; inspect dashboard and lists; maintain staff or account status; 
review appointments and charges; choose report filters; inspect or export the results.

2 Requirement Determination and Analysis 
Requirement analysis connects the purpose of the project to operations that can be inspected 
and tested. The functional baseline is the current application: its URL configuration, views, 
templates, models, migrations and existing tests. Requirements below distinguish 
implemented behaviour from recommended acceptance targets. They do not claim that 
stakeholder interviews, surveys or hospital observations were performed. 
The requirements are organised around the four roles and the records they exchange. Each 
requirement has an identifier so that a reviewer can connect it to a design element and a test. 
A requirement described as implemented means that a corresponding source path exists; it 
does not mean that every branch has been executed successfully in a live deployment. 
2.1 Requirement Determination 
Method and evidence sources 
The analysis began with the repository structure and the root routing configuration. The 
patient URL file identifies public pages, authentication and self service functions. The doctor, 
receptionist and adminpanel route files identify staff operations. The functions reached by 
those routes provide the authoritative behaviour when older project prose disagrees with 
implementation comments or templates. 
Models and migrations establish persistent data and changes over time. Template fields 
identify the information users are asked to supply, while views determine what is actually 
checked and saved. Existing automated tests provide executable examples of selected 
workflows. Deployment files explain intended hosting arrangements, but a configuration 
template is not evidence that a service has been installed or operated successfully. 
The retained project report provides academic identity details and reference screenshots. It is 
not treated as stronger evidence than the current source for feature claims. In particular, the 
card form is not a gateway integration and the patient portal does not currently expose a 
dedicated prescription history route.

Workflow and data analysis 
The patient booking workflow has three distinct stages: selecting a slot, reviewing the fee and 
submitting checkout. The first stage validates a candidate and stores pending details in the 
session. The review page displays those details. Only checkout submission creates the 
appointment. This distinction is a requirement because treating the earlier session entry as a 
persistent reservation would overstate what the system guarantees. 
The receptionist workflow differs deliberately. Reception is assisting a patient in person, so a 
valid booking directly creates an appointment with confirmed status and a pending 
consultation bill. Confirmation, cancellation and no show are subsequent actions. Their side 
effects include patient notifications, selected emails and, for a no show, an additional fee 
equal to the consultation fee. 
The doctor workflow begins with assigned visits and related patients. Clinical records contain 
a diagnosis and optional advice, follow up date and appointment link. Medicine rows are 
repeating detail records. A linked appointment is rechecked against both the doctor and 
patient to reject a forged association. The data requirement is therefore stronger than merely 
accepting an appointment identifier from a dropdown. 
Administrator workflows operate across the hospital data set. Lists and report filters use 
dates, statuses, doctors, departments and search terms where implemented. The same report 
selection can produce an HTML view, CSV file or PDF file. Billing reports use appointment 
dates for their date range, a detail that must be understood before comparing them with 
reports based on bill creation time.

Technical feasibility 
The technical stack is feasible for an academic web application because the repository 
already contains working Django apps, migrations, templates and a configured project 
environment. The existing tests create an isolated schema and exercise portal pages and 
workflow updates. The source uses standard relational models and framework authentication 
rather than requiring a separately deployed identity service. 
The local database guide describes a standalone MySQL installation, while 
DATABASE_URL permits another configured backend and an SQLite fallback. This makes 
development flexible, but it creates a verification obligation. The serialisation provided by 
select_for_update must be evaluated with the actual database engine; SQLite does not 
provide equivalent row locking semantics. 
The frontend depends on browser support for JavaScript and some CDN assets. PDF export 
depends on ReportLab and valid layout data. Uploaded profile images depend on writable file 
storage and Pillow validation. Technical readiness therefore includes checking dependencies, 
static collection, mail settings, file permissions and database connectivity in the intended 
environment. 
Operational feasibility 
Operationally, the portal structure maps to recognisable responsibilities: patients manage 
their own visits, reception coordinates arrival and payment, doctors maintain consultation 
information, and administrators manage wider records. A training demonstration can follow 
one patient from registration to booking, reception confirmation, doctor prescription and final 
receipt. 
Operational readiness still requires decisions beyond the source. The hospital would need 
rules for who may create or deactivate accounts, how a mistaken bill is corrected, how 
appointment cancellations affect payments and how records are retained. The application 
does not implement an organisational approval workflow for those decisions. A real 
deployment would also need an operator to monitor mail failures, back up media and 
databases and restore a tested copy when required. 
Economic feasibility 
The application uses an open source programming language and framework, so the academic 
implementation does not inherently require a commercial web framework licence. That 
observation is not a complete cost estimate. Hosting, domain registration, operational 
support, secure mail delivery, backups, staff training and future maintenance all consume 
resources. 
No purchase quotations, staff time measurements or approved budget were supplied. 
Accordingly, economic feasibility is described through cost categories rather than invented 
currency totals or claimed savings. A later pilot should measure registration time, failed 
booking attempts, reporting effort and support incidents before estimating financial benefit.

Constraints and assumptions 
The application assumes that a role account has the matching role profile where required. 
Some helper views create or retrieve profiles defensively; other operations retrieve an 
existing profile directly. Account creation and migrations therefore matter to workflow 
correctness. The report does not assume that every arbitrary user row can immediately use 
every role portal. 
The system also assumes that consultation fees and schedule parameters are meaningful. 
Positive model fields and form checks help, but a complete boundary review should include 
zero duration, unusual buffer values, large fees and invalid choice strings. Server side checks 
must remain authoritative because clients can bypass HTML constraints and JavaScript. 
The current code is a synchronous application. Mail attempts and report generation occur 
within request or command flows rather than a verified background worker architecture. 
Proposed queues, caching and monitoring appear in Chapter 6 as enhancements. They are not 
presented as existing runtime services.

Requirement dependencies and priority 
Identity and role checks precede every protected workflow. Patient and doctor profiles 
precede appointment creation, and an appointment precedes a consultation bill. Prescription 
entry depends on the doctor to patient relationship and optionally on the exact appointment. 
Reports depend on the operational record definitions, so their correctness cannot be assessed 
only by whether a file downloads. 
The first acceptance priority is preventing unauthorised access and incorrect core writes. The 
second is validating complete booking, consultation and billing workflows. The third is 
verifying output parity, responsive presentation and operational recovery. New functionality 
should not displace these checks merely because a screen appears complete.

3 System Design 
System design translates requirements into actors, records, request flows and user interfaces. 
The project follows Django's model, template and view organisation. Its logical boundaries 
are shared identity, role specific workflows, persistent domain models and output helpers. 
These boundaries are implemented within one application deployment rather than as 
independent microservices. 
The diagrams below are derived from current relationships and view behaviour. They 
describe the design at a readable level and do not imply components absent from the 
repository. The sequence and activity figures are numbered workflow abstractions; the code 
references identify the exact implementation for detailed review.

Integrity rules and normalisation 
Identity and role profiles are separated to avoid repeating password and role data in each 
domain table. Appointment references patient and doctor profiles rather than copying full 
demographic records into every visit. PrescriptionMedicine removes the need for a fixed set 
of medicine columns and allows a prescription to contain several detail rows. 
Some redundancy remains purposeful but requires care. Billing stores patient separately from 
appointment even though the appointment already identifies the patient. Appointment stores a 
department value even though its doctor also has a department. These values should be 
treated as explicit business data whose consistency or historical meaning must be defined; 
they should not be assumed to synchronise automatically after a profile change. 
CASCADE deletion can remove substantial related history. For example, deleting a patient 
profile can remove appointments and bills and also prescriptions through their patient 
reference. This differs from deactivating the linked account, which changes login eligibility

without deleting those domain rows. An operational deployment should prefer a defined 
retention and archival policy rather than casual physical deletion. 
Framework support tables include sessions, authentication groups and permissions, content 
types and Django administration logs. User has inherited many to many relationships to 
groups and user_permissions, represented by junction tables. These structures support the 
framework; the custom portal authorisation primarily reads the role field and its view 
decorators. 
3.3 User Interface Design 
The application uses a public patient themed base template and separate staff portal base 
templates. Bootstrap provides layout utilities and components, while role specific CSS 
supplies visual identity. Staff portals use navigation sidebars and top bars; patient pages use 
the public site navigation and focused dashboard panels. Forms submit to Django views and 
include CSRF tokens where defined.

Initialisation and request processing 
manage.py sets the configuration module and invokes Django command execution. WSGI 
and ASGI entry modules expose the application for server integration. Root routing includes 
the patient routes at the site root and the other portals under their prefixes. The framework 
admin has a separate /admin/ path. 
Middleware order matters. Security and WhiteNoise precede session and authentication 
handling; CSRF middleware protects participating unsafe requests; message middleware 
supports validation feedback; clickjacking middleware provides the configured response 
protection. The request reaches a view only after URL matching. A role decorator then 
decides whether the authenticated user may proceed.

Templates receive view context and global context processor values. Portal notification 
processors contribute unread counts. Static template tags resolve frontend assets according to 
storage configuration. Development uses finder based static handling when DEBUG is true, 
while production configuration selects compressed manifest storage and expects collectstatic 
output.

Name validation is implemented by a small regular expression helper that accepts the 
supported letters, spaces, apostrophes and hyphens. It improves data format checks but does 
not prove legal identity or support every writing system. Broader multilingual support would 
require an explicit product decision and suitable tests.

the profile field.

requirement. Unknown route names, unsafe external targets and unrecognised relative paths 
fall back to a named destination. This avoids malformed concatenated appointment

Results and observations 
The executed evidence supports the redirect correction and selected core portal workflows. In 
particular, confirmation can return correctly from both receptionist appointment lists, 
sequential duplicate slots are rejected, repeated no show handling does not add another fee in 
the checked path, and permitted details and receipts render in the isolated fixture. 
The suite is not exhaustive. It does not execute real OTP interaction, browser JavaScript, 
production email delivery, MySQL row lock contention or large report output. It also does not 
establish complete branch coverage or prove that all malformed inputs are handled without 
server errors. The proposed acceptance cases identify concrete gaps rather than representing 
them as passed. 
The appropriate release judgement is that the current automated baseline is passing in its 
documented test environment. Broader operational approval requires the additional checks 
selected for the deployment and its data sensitivity. Test evidence should be refreshed after 
source, dependency or environment changes rather than copied indefinitely from this report.

6 Proposed Enhancements 
The proposed enhancements address gaps visible in the implementation and opportunities that 
follow from the present scope. They are future work. None of the items in this chapter should 
be interpreted as a feature already delivered by the current source. 
Complete transaction units 
Group appointment, bill and notification creation within one reviewed transaction, and trigger 
external messages after commit. Apply the same principle to prescription header and medicine 
detail creation. 
Reason: A failure between separate writes can currently leave incomplete related state. The 
improvement should include injected failure tests and an explicit retry strategy rather than 
simply adding a broad try/except. 
Completion criterion: Verify that every injected write failure leaves either the complete 
operation or no operation, and that mail is not sent for a rolled back booking. 
Database backed booking integrity 
Define a database appropriate invariant for active slot occupancy and retain row locking for 
the supported workflows. Consider a dedicated slot or reservation model if future scheduling 
requires multiple resources. 
Reason: The current Appointment model lacks a doctor/date/slot unique constraint, and a 
naive unconditional constraint would conflict with cancelled history. Design must preserve 
the ability to rebook a cancelled slot. 
Completion criterion: Run concurrent requests on the deployment database and confirm at 
most one active reservation, including cancellation and rebooking sequences. 
Unified schedule and timezone rules 
Use a shared default schedule for the availability form and slot algorithm, and centralise 
timezone aware date/time calculations. Validate duration, buffer and cap consistently before 
saving. 
Reason: The unsaved availability form defaults to a shorter Saturday and closed Sunday, 
while the model fallback opens missing days 09:00 to 17:00. Naive local calculations can 
disagree with UTC configuration around date boundaries. 
Completion criterion: Compare form display and JSON slots for every unconfigured weekday 
and test hospital midnight boundary cases. 
Authentication hardening 
Introduce server enforced resend and login limits, consider hashed OTP storage and add a 
complete password/OTP test suite. Record delivery errors without exposing codes in logs. 
Reason: The displayed resend cooldown is not enough to prove a backend rate limit, and 
existing force_login tests bypass the actual login journey. Optional OTP policy should remain 
an explicit administrative decision. 
Completion criterion: Verify lockout, expiry, repeated resend, replay, inactive accounts and 
reset link handling through controlled sessions.

Reusable validation and services 
Introduce Django forms or equivalent validated input objects for repeated account, schedule, 
prescription and billing data. Centralise named business operations and their side effects. 
Reason: Many views read raw POST dictionaries. Model choices do not automatically 
validate values during save, and parallel medicine arrays can be inconsistent. Shared services 
would reduce divergence between portals. 
Completion criterion: Use boundary tests for required values, numeric ranges, choices and 
related identifiers, then compare equivalent workflows across roles. 
Patient prescription access 
Add an explicitly authorised patient prescription history and download flow with doctor 
attribution and medicine details. Define what clinical information may be shown and when. 
Reason: Current doctor routes provide prescription entry and history, but a dedicated patient 
prescription route was not found. The enhancement should therefore be implemented and 
tested before being advertised. 
Completion criterion: A patient can retrieve only personal published clinical documents; 
another patients identifier is rejected. 
Real payment integration 
Replace the demonstration checkout with a selected gateway integration using server side 
verification, signed webhooks, idempotency and reconciliation. Define cancellation and 
refund policy. 
Reason: The current card form does not validate, store or charge card data. A paid database 
status from that flow is an educational simulation. Financial state should be separated from 
appointment workflow. 
Completion criterion: Test sandbox success, declined payment, timeout, duplicate webhook, 
delayed settlement and refund without storing sensitive card credentials. 
Auditing and record retention 
Add immutable application audit events for clinical, account, appointment and billing 
changes, and define retention and archival policies. Prefer controlled deactivation to 
unreviewed deletion. 
Reason: created_at and updated_at record times but not complete actor and prior state history. 
Cascading deletion can remove substantial related records. 
Completion criterion: Reconstruct an authorised state change from the audit trail and confirm 
that archival and restore preserve required relationships. 
Reporting correctness and scale 
Validate all filter inputs, show only filters actually applied, distinguish paid revenue from 
total charges and add bounded or background exports for large data sets. Handle spreadsheet 
formula prefixes safely.

Reason: The doctor report ignores date inputs, billing ranges use visit dates and matched 
billing totals are not automatically collected revenue. Exports materialise complete row lists 
in memory. 
Completion criterion: Compare cross format outputs, test long fields and malformed filters, 
and measure memory and latency at the intended volume. 
Observable messaging and background work 
Add a delivery record, retry policy and background queue for appointment communication 
and reminders. Install and monitor an explicit scheduler with documented ownership. 
Reason: Appointment email sends can fail silently, and reminder_sent can be set after an 
unsuccessful attempt. A launcher file alone does not prove a running schedule. 
Completion criterion: Simulate transport outage, verify retries and failure visibility, and 
confirm that only genuinely processed or delivered states receive their intended flag. 
Operational deployment and recovery 
Automate configuration checks, release tests, health monitoring and database/media backup 
restoration in a separate environment. Review secure hosting settings and access management. 
Reason: The repository contains deployment templates, not a measured uptime result or a 
completed restore programme. A documented clean dependency installation should resolve 
installed versus pinned differences. 
Completion criterion: Run a reproducible staging release and restore rehearsal and record the 
actual recovery time and remaining manual steps. 
Usability and inclusive access 
Perform keyboard, screen reader and small screen testing; improve focus, field errors and 
terminology based on observed task completion. Consider local asset hosting and broader 
name support. 
Reason: Bootstrap responsiveness and supplied screenshots do not establish accessibility 
conformance. CDN dependencies and a restricted name expression can affect particular users 
or environments. 
Completion criterion: Complete role based tasks with assistive interaction and record usability 
defects and verified corrections.

7 Conclusion 
The Hospital Management System demonstrates how a common relational application can 
connect outpatient administration and doctor consultation work. The original problem is the 
effort and inconsistency that can arise when patient identity, doctor schedules, visits and 
charges are maintained in disconnected places. The implemented solution gives these records 
explicit relationships and presents them through four role focused portals. 
Patients can register, maintain their profiles, discover doctors, select consultation slots and 
inspect personal appointments and bills. Receptionists can register walk in patients, search 
existing records, create confirmed visits, manage attendance and record bill payment. Doctors 
can maintain availability, review related patients and write diagnoses and medicine details. 
Administrators can manage staff access, inspect hospital wide operational lists, control the 
OTP policy and generate reports. 
The project uses Python and Django with server rendered templates, shared authentication, 
framework sessions and an environment selected relational database. The model structure 
separates User from role profiles, appointments from bills and prescription headers from 
medicine lines. Shared helpers support slot generation, pagination, upload checks and safe 
return navigation. Management reports support browser display, CSV and ReportLab PDF, 
while individual receipts use browser print layouts. 
Several objectives are demonstrated by specific code and passing test assertions. The existing 
thirteen tests passed in an isolated SQLite environment on 20 October 2026. They checked 
safe redirects, selected appointment transitions, sequential duplicate booking rejection, 
assisted registration and search, notifications and permitted page rendering. Framework 
checks, the migration dry run and the installed dependency check also completed 
successfully. 
These results have practical limits. They do not establish live MySQL concurrency, browser 
accessibility, external email reliability or production recovery. The card checkout is simulated 
and must not be treated as a real financial gateway. Dedicated patient prescription access is a 
future capability, not an existing route. The current transaction boundaries and direct POST 
handling also leave clear opportunities for stronger consistency and validation. 
The application is useful as an academic demonstration of integrated role based web 
development and outpatient workflow modelling. Its value lies in the connection between 
requirements, data design, views, templates and testable outcomes. Further work should first 
strengthen core integrity, scheduling consistency, authentication and operational observability 
before expanding the functional scope. A wider deployment should be accepted against 
controlled end to end and environment specific tests rather than inferred from the existence of 
complete looking screens.
